'''David Zitoun''' ({{langx|he|דוד זיתון}}) is an Israeli [[chemist]] and [[Materials science|materials scientist]].

==Biography==
David Zitoun<ref name="BIU">{{Cite web |title=Zitoun David {{!}} Department of Chemistry |url=https://ch.biu.ac.il/zitoun |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=ch.biu.ac.il}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. David Zitoun – David Zitoun's Lab |url=https://www.zitounlab.com/people/dr-david-zitoun/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |language=en-US}}</ref> obtained his M.Sc. (1999) in [[Physical chemistry]] from [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|Ecole Normale Superieure]], [[France]], and a Ph.D. (2003) from the [[Paul Sabatier University|University Toulouse III]], France, under the supervision of Bruno Chaudret, with a dissertation on the [[magnetism]] of [[Nanoparticle|clusters]].<ref name="Muñoz-NaviaDorantes-Dávila2008">{{cite journal|last1=Muñoz-Navia|first1=M.|last2=Dorantes-Dávila|first2=J.|last3=Zitoun|first3=D.|last4=Amiens|first4=C.|last5=Chaudret|first5=B.|last6=Casanove|first6=M.-J.|last7=Lecante|first7=P.|last8=Jaouen|first8=N.|last9=Rogalev|first9=A.|last10=Respaud|first10=M.|last11=Pastor|first11=G. M.|title=Magnetic properties of CoNRhMnanoparticles: experiment and theory|journal=Faraday Discuss.|volume=138|year=2008|pages=181–192|issn=1359-6640|doi=10.1039/B705122K|pmid=18447016}}</ref>  In 2003 he was a Post-Doctoral Research Fellow at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] with Prof. [[Peidong Yang]], investigating the [[Magnetic semiconductor|diluted magnetic semiconducting]] [[nanowire]]s.<ref name="YuhasZitoun2006">{{cite journal|last1=Yuhas|first1=Benjamin D.|last2=Zitoun|first2=David O.|last3=Pauzauskie|first3=Peter J.|last4=He|first4=Rongrui|last5=Yang|first5=Peidong|title=Transition-Metal Doped Zinc Oxide Nanowires|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=45|issue=3|year=2006|pages=420–423|issn=1433-7851|doi=10.1002/anie.200503172|pmid=16342314}}</ref> Between 2004 and 2009 he was a senior lecturer at [[Montpellier 2 University]], France, and in 2009 he joined the Department of Chemistry<ref name=BIU /> at [[Bar-Ilan University]] (BIU) where he is currently a full professor and holds the position of the Head of the department.<ref name=head>[https://ch.biu.ac.il/faculty Department of Chemistry, Bar-Ilan University]</ref> Zitoun is a member of the Bar-Ilan Institute for [[Nanotechnology]] and Advanced Materials (BINA),<ref>[https://nano.biu.ac.il/ Bar Ilan's Institute for Nanotechnology and Advanced Materials (BINA)]</ref> a member of the Israel National Research Center for [[Electrochemistry|Electrochemical]] [[Propulsion]] (INREP),<ref>[http://inrep.org.il/ Israel National Research Center for Electrochemical Propulsion]</ref> an associate editor of the ''[[Journal of Nanoparticle Research]]'' ([[Springer Publishing|Springer]]), a Panel Member of the FORMAS Funding Agency (Sweden),<ref>[https://formas.se/en/start-page/about-formas.html Formas - a government research council for sustainable development]</ref> and an Expert for the [[Framework Programmes for Research and Technological Development#Horizon 2020|Horizon 2020]] research program. He has also been a consultant for [[Israel Chemicals|ICL-IP]], PVNanoCell, and CENS Materials.

== Scientific interests and publications ==
His current research<ref name=BIU /><ref>[https://zitounlab.com/publications/ David Zitoun's Nanomaterials on Surfaces Lab - List of Publications]</ref> focuses on the investigation of the [[Materials science#Synthesis and processing|chemical synthesis of materials]] to promote [[Renewable energy|renewable and green energies]]. Zitoun's lab has a high expertise in the [[Wet chemistry|wet synthesis]] of [[Nanomaterials|Nano-scale materials]] with the accent on the [[transition metal]]s, their [[Coordination complex|complexes]], [[Organometallic chemistry|organometallic]], [[Intermetallic|metallic]], and [[Oxide#Oxides of metals|metal-oxide]] [[Chemical compound|compounds]]. He developed new chemical routes using soluble organometallic<ref name="ShviroZitoun2012">{{cite journal|last1=Shviro|first1=Meital|last2=Zitoun|first2=David|title=Low temperature, template-free route to nickel thin films and nanowires|journal=Nanoscale|volume=4|issue=3|year=2012|pages=762–767|issn=2040-3364|doi=10.1039/C1NR11177A}}</ref> or [[Metal-organic compound|metal-organic precursors]]<ref name="ShviroPolani2015">{{cite journal|last1=Shviro|first1=Meital|last2=Polani|first2=Shlomi|last3=Zitoun|first3=David|title=Hollow octahedral and cuboctahedral nanocrystals of ternary Pt–Ni–Au alloys|journal=Nanoscale|volume=7|issue=32|year=2015|pages=13521–13529|issn=2040-3364|doi=10.1039/C5NR03522H}}</ref> as an alternative to conventional [[Colloid|colloidal chemistry]] and gas phase [[Thin film#Chemical deposition|thin film deposition]]. The [[nanomaterials]] exhibit high activity for electrocatalysis in alkaline medium.<ref name="BakosPaszternák2015">{{cite journal|last1=Bakos|first1=István|last2=Paszternák|first2=András|last3=Zitoun|first3=David|title=Pd/Ni Synergestic Activity for Hydrogen Oxidation Reaction in Alkaline Conditions|journal=Electrochimica Acta|volume=176|year=2015|pages=1074–1082|issn=0013-4686|doi=10.1016/j.electacta.2015.07.109|url=http://real.mtak.hu/25806/1/PdNi_Ms_2015_07_17_revised2.pdf}}</ref><ref name="AleskerPage2016">{{cite journal|last1=Alesker|first1=Maria|last2=Page|first2=Miles|last3=Shviro|first3=Meital|last4=Paska|first4=Yair|last5=Gershinsky|first5=Gregory|last6=Dekel|first6=Dario R.|last7=Zitoun|first7=David|title=Palladium/nickel bifunctional electrocatalyst for hydrogen oxidation reaction in alkaline membrane fuel cell|journal=Journal of Power Sources|volume=304|year=2016|pages=332–339|issn=0378-7753|doi=10.1016/j.jpowsour.2015.11.026}}</ref> Zitoun and colleagues were the first to introduce the use of [[Electron magnetic moment#Measurement|electron magnetic measurements]] in post-mortem analyses of [[Lithium-ion battery|Li-ion batteries]]<ref name="BoyanovWomes2009">{{cite journal|last1=Boyanov|first1=S.|last2=Womes|first2=M.|last3=Monconduit|first3=L.|last4=Zitoun|first4=D.|title=Mössbauer Spectroscopy and Magnetic Measurements As Complementary Techniques for the Phase Analysis of FeP Electrodes Cycling in Li-Ion Batteries|journal=Chemistry of Materials|volume=21|issue=15|year=2009|pages=3684–3692|issn=0897-4756|doi=10.1021/cm901243a}}</ref> and the first group to publish the [[Operando spectroscopy|operando]] electron magnetic measurements.<ref name="GershinskyBar2014">{{cite journal|last1=Gershinsky|first1=Gregory|last2=Bar|first2=Elad|last3=Monconduit|first3=Laure|last4=Zitoun|first4=David|title=Operando electron magnetic measurements of Li-ion batteries|journal=Energy Environ. Sci.|volume=7|issue=6|year=2014|pages=2012–2016|issn=1754-5692|doi=10.1039/C4EE00490F}}</ref> These [[In situ|in-situ]] measurements allowed proposing a new [[Electrochemical reaction mechanism|electrochemical mechanism]] for the high energy density [[Galvanic anode#Anode materials|anodic materials]]. David Zitoun has an active scientific collaboration with many world-renowned scientists, among which are Prof. [[Doron Aurbach]], Prof. [[Zeev Zalevsky]] and Prof. [[Nicola Pinna]].

==Personal life==
David Zitoun is married to Keren Zitoun, a [[pharmacist]] with a thesis in [[music therapy]]. They [[Aliyah|immigrated to Israel]] in 2009<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-07-12 |title=French success |url=https://www.jpost.com/Magazine/Features/French-success |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en |issn=0792-822X}}</ref> and have four children.
